summary: Created a CA named "Fleet Internal CA" on node1 (OpenSSL, 4096-bit RSA, self-signed, CN=Fleet Internal CA, 10y validity), issued a 2048-bit TLS server cert to node2 (CN=node2, SAN=DNS:node2,IP:10.100.160.11, signed by the CA), configured nginx on node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with that cert+key, and installed the CA cert into the system trust store on both node1 and node2 via update-ca-certificates. Verified end-to-end: curl to https://10.100.160.11:8443 succeeds with full chain validation from both nodes using only system trust (no --cacert needed). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured boot_id baselines, rebooted node1 then node2 sequentially, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed post-restart recovery (CA files/keys intact on node1, SSH connectivity restored; nginx auto-started and HTTPS/CA trust fully functional on node2) before proceeding to the next node.
actions_performed: Generated CA private key and self-signed CA certificate (CN=Fleet Internal CA) on node1 under ~/ca
Generated node2 key, CSR (CN=node2, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.160.11), and signed it with the CA producing a valid, chain-verified certificate
Installed nginx on node2 (apt-get) and configured it to listen on 8443 with the issued cert+key
Transferred CA cert, node2 cert, and node2 key from node1 to node2 over inter-node SSH using the cluster keypair
Installed the CA cert as a trusted system CA (update-ca-certificates) on both node1 and node2
Verified TLS handshake and chain-of-trust from both nodes using only system trust store (no manual --cacert)
Captured boot_id and health baselines on both nodes prior to restart
Rebooted node1, polled until SSH/exec available, confirmed changed boot_id, verified CA files intact and TLS trust functional
Rebooted node2, polled until SSH/exec available, confirmed changed boot_id, verified nginx auto-started, HTTPS on 8443 live, and CA trust functional
